title: MOFA welcomes reaffirmation of importance of peace and stability across Taiwan Strait by US, Japan, and ROK foreign ministers
text:
Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung welcomes the reaffirmation of the importance of peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait by the US, Japanese, and Republic of Korea foreign ministers on October 30. Minister Lin encourages partner countries to continue taking concrete action to safeguard overall peace and stability in the region.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Japanese Minister for Foreign Affairs Toshimitsu Motegi, and ROK Minister of Foreign Affairs Cho Hyun expressed the aforementioned position at a trilateral gathering held on the sidelines of the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta.

Following the gathering, the US Department of State issued a press release. In addition to stressing the importance of cross-strait peace and stability, the press release conveyed concern regarding China’s efforts to assert control over the South China Sea, its coercive behavior in the East China Sea and the Yellow Sea, and the negative impacts of China-Russia cooperation in the Indo-Pacific, which is undermining peace and stability.

The US, Japan, and ROK foreign ministers have publicly reiterated the importance of upholding cross-strait peace and stability on numerous occasions this year, underscoring that the security of the Taiwan Strait is critical to regional stability. This has become a shared, high-priority issue for the international community and is indispensable to peace and prosperity across the Indo-Pacific.

In response to China’s ongoing escalation of military threats and gray-zone intrusions, Taiwan will steadily deepen cooperation with the United States and other like-minded nations to jointly ensure peace, stability, and prosperity across the Taiwan Strait and the Indo-Pacific. (E)
